Maker adapter state and the remaining pDAI routes
4 October 2026. Getter and runtime-code reads only. No transactions, state overrides or execution
simulations.
Finding
The USDC adapter ending 2199 is live at this checkpoint; Maker's Vat remains shut down.
Ordinary PSM conversion is therefore disabled. Existing savings-credit conversion and possible shutdown
collateral settlement are separate routes with different rights and conditions.
The exact adapter is AuthGemJoin5, 0x0a59649758aa4d66e25f08dd01271e891fe52199. It is not DaiJoin, which is 
0x9759a6ac90977b93b58547b4a71c78317f391a28.
At PulseChain chain 369, block 27,707,510, hash 
0x8a99d5ac2c73089e006d50765bbfaa5d92e6fb523fb6d5384a2c100794cfb63b, timestamp 4 October 2026, 01:39:15
UTC:
Getter Result and meaning
Vat.live() 0. Ordinary PSM operations encounter the shutdown check
in Vat.frob.
USDC adapter live() 1. The adapter's own deposit-live gate is enabled; this
does not bypass Vat shutdown.
DaiJoin.live() 1. Its exit-live gate remains enabled.
End.live() 0. Maker is in the shutdown regime; selected settlement
functions have separate accounting conditions.
USDC adapter vat() / gem() / dec() Exact inherited Vat, exact copied pUSDC and six decimals.
USDC adapter wards(PSM) 1. The PSM retains adapter deposit authorization; ordinary
conversion still fails at Vat.
pDAI wards(DaiJoin) 1. DaiJoin retains token-mint authority.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 304

Getter Result and meaning
pUSDC held by the USDC adapter 113,692,361.975557 pUSDC. Physical custody is not
every caller's redeemable balance.
Vat.gem(PSM-USDC-A, End) 0. No internal collateral is allocated to End at this location.
Why a caged collateral adapter need not block exit
The matched AuthGemJoin5 source checks live == 1 in its authorized three-argument join. Its public exit
has no live check: it debits the caller's internal collateral through Vat.slip and transfers the
corresponding pUSDC. Consequently, a hypothetical adapter cage would block new deposits while
retaining this exit path under its other conditions.
Those conditions include internal collateral credit, the adapter's Vat authorization, sufficient physical
tokens and functioning token transfers. Exit does not make the entire adapter balance freely
withdrawable. DaiJoin differs: its exit expressly requires its own live == 1, caller credit and the required
Vat permission. The public USDC adapter source documents the design; the saved matched source and
runtime checks establish the examined local implementation.
Route conclusions
Route Conclusion
DOLA sale → pUSDC → ordinary PSM → newly minted pDAI Historically executed; disabled by Vat shutdown at the
fresh checkpoint, regardless of the adapter's live flag.
Owned sDAI/Pot credit → DaiJoin exit → pDAI Historical post-shutdown execution is demonstrated. It
converts existing credit and consumes the relevant claim;
it is not unrestricted new credit or proof of continuing
savings yield.
Process PSM collateral → End claim → USDC adapter exit A source-supported conditional settlement proposal.
Allocation and actual payout are unproven; the fresh End
collateral getter remains zero. The prior prorated
settlement rate is not a one-for-one conversion.
Existing authorized contract → Vat.suck → eligible DaiJoin
exit
Separate authority-dependent possibility creating credit
and corresponding debt. No usable group-controlled
arbitrary issuance path is demonstrated.
Funded markets paying already existing pDAI Separate market route, subject to actual liquidity and
costs; does not require ordinary Maker PSM issuance.
The arbitrage and shutdown study (Appendix 25) retains actual trades, prior credit balances, source
matches and proposed settlement arithmetic. This new checkpoint updates selected adapter flags,
identities, custody and allocation only; it does not refresh all earlier claims or prove settlement
execution.
Economic relevance
The recorded settlement rate is 0.000879277935257435670774324 pUSDC per pDAI. It pays about
879.277935 pUSDC for one million pDAI, subject to processing, eligibility and rounding. At equal
accounting value per normalized pStable, this returns 0.0879278% of input value before costs, a
difference of approximately 99.9121%. The issue is the low payout per claim, rather than the adapter's
physical balance alone.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 305

A fresh trade could be rational if the complete pDAI acquisition and settlement cost were below the
pUSDC-equivalent payout, using executable market values. An already packed eligible claim may also
have recoverable value without a new pDAI purchase. These are conditional economic cases, not
observed use or proof of recurring capacity. For the stabilization thesis, retain this as a low-priority
legacy settlement possibility, not a credible equal-parity funding engine at the recorded rate.
Verification and reproduction
Fourteen explicit getter/code jobs generated 23 read-only RPC records, including selector derivation and
matching block-header rechecks. Every request returned without an RPC error. Fresh Vat, DaiJoin and
USDC-adapter runtimes exactly equal the corresponding saved runtimes used in the earlier source audit.
AuthGemJoin5 join/exit/cage and Vat slip/frob checks were inspected offline.
The explicit manifest is pulsechain_maker_adapter_closure_20261004.json. Raw reads, decoded
verification, frozen paper input/output and hashes are in artifacts/pulsechain-maker-adapter-
closure-20261004/. Earlier batches are unchanged. Always use the explicit getter manifest with the probe;
its broader discovery default includes operations outside this read-only scope.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 306
